name: PM-KISAN (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi)
description: Direct income support of ₹6,000 per year to small and marginal farmer families, paid in three installments of ₹2,000 each.
eligibility: All farmer families with cultivable land holdings. Excluded: Institutional land holders, former/present ministers, income tax payers, professionals (doctors, engineers, lawyers, CAs).
benefits: ₹6,000/year directly credited to bank account in 3 installments of ₹2,000 each (April-July, August-November, December-March).
how_to_apply: Visit pmkisan.gov.in → New Registration → Enter Aadhaar, bank details, land records. OR visit local CSC (Common Service Centre).

name: PMFBY (Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana)
description: Comprehensive crop insurance scheme providing financial support to farmers suffering crop loss/damage due to natural calamities, pests, and diseases.
eligibility: All farmers growing notified crops. Mandatory for loanee farmers, optional for non-loanee farmers.
benefits: Insurance coverage at very low premium: 2% for Kharif crops, 1.5% for Rabi crops, 5% for commercial/horticultural crops. Government pays remaining premium.
how_to_apply: Apply through any bank branch, CSC center, or online at pmfby.gov.in within the notification period. Requires land ownership proof, Aadhaar, bank details.

name: Kisan Credit Card (KCC)
description: Provides adequate and timely credit support to farmers for their agricultural needs including crop production, post-harvest expenses, farm maintenance, and allied activities.
eligibility: All farmers, sharecroppers, tenant farmers, self-help groups, joint liability groups.
benefits: Credit limit based on land holding and crop pattern. Interest rate: 7% (with 3% subvention = effective 4% for timely repayment). Animal husbandry and fisheries now included.
how_to_apply: Apply at any commercial bank, cooperative bank, or regional rural bank. Take: Land documents, Aadhaar, photo, bank passbook.

name: Soil Health Card Scheme
description: Provides soil health cards to farmers with information on nutrient status of their soil along with recommendations on appropriate dosage of nutrients for improving soil health and fertility.
benefits: Free soil testing every 2 years. Crop-wise nutrient recommendations. Helps optimize fertilizer use and reduce costs.
how_to_apply: Contact local agriculture department or Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK). Soil samples are collected and tested at government labs.

name: PM Krishi Sinchai Yojana (PMKSY)
description: Aims to ensure access to some means of protective irrigation to all agricultural farms (Har Khet Ko Paani) and improve water use efficiency (More Crop Per Drop) through micro-irrigation.
eligibility: All farmers, with priority to small and marginal farmers. Land ownership documents required.
benefits: 55% subsidy for small/marginal farmers, 45% for others on micro-irrigation (drip and sprinkler) equipment.
how_to_apply: Apply through district agriculture office or state agriculture portal. Submit: Land documents, Aadhaar, water source proof.

name: e-NAM (National Agriculture Market)
description: Pan-India electronic trading portal linking existing APMC mandis to create a unified national market for agricultural commodities.
eligibility: All farmers, traders, commission agents, and processors.
benefits: Better price discovery through transparent auction. Direct sale to buyers across India. Reduced intermediaries. Online payment and quality assaying.
how_to_apply: Register at enam.gov.in with Aadhaar and bank details. Can also register at nearest e-NAM enabled mandi.

name: Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY)
description: Promotes organic farming through adoption of organic village clusters. Farmers are provided financial assistance for organic inputs, certification, and marketing.
eligibility: Groups of 50+ farmers forming a cluster of 50 acres. Priority to women farmers and SC/ST farmers.
benefits: ₹50,000/hectare over 3 years for organic inputs, seeds, and marketing. PGS (Participatory Guarantee System) certification.
how_to_apply: Form a cluster of 50 farmers with 50 acres. Apply through state agriculture department or visit pgsindia-ncof.gov.in.

name: National Mission on Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA)
description: Aims to make agriculture more productive, sustainable, and climate resilient through improved production practices, soil health management, and water use efficiency.
eligibility: All farmers, particularly those in rainfed areas.
benefits: Subsidies on: Micro-irrigation, soil testing, organic manure production, climate resilient crop varieties.
how_to_apply: Contact district agriculture office. Projects are implemented through state agriculture departments.
